route.change: Think-SFT with the cue, cap raised from 16,384 to 32,768, two samples per problem, kept by a fixed selection rule: if both finish and agree take that answer, if one hits the cap take the finished one, if both finish and differ take the shorter (rule fixed before any scoring).
route.gap_parts: Budget (cap hit): about a quarter of the gap (result-f39ba8: .25 of 65 on MATH-500 T 1.0, about 16 answers; .27 on hard328). Think-SFT turns about one in four of its cap hits into right answers at 32k (207 -> 230 on hard328), and the finished-over-cap-hit rule recovers more when one of two samples runs out. Reliability (.63 of the gap, about 41 answers on MATH-500): the second sample with the shorter-finished tie rule wins back part of the problems the model solves in some samples (wrong samples run about 2,300 tokens longer). Capability (about .09-.27) is not touched.
route.why: A capped count scores unfinished work as wrong, and Think-SFT has the largest share of unfinished-work cap hits (about one in four, against one in ten for RL), so a higher cap plus a rule that keeps the finished sample should help Think-SFT most. Two samples rather than four keeps the cost under the 241-at-30,904 vote, and stays below the pass@4 ceiling where extra samples stop adding (round-10/grader-m06).
